// p3poll is F5's witness (Burroughs #1240): goroutines that block on their own. Built for the fork's
// GOOS=wasip3, an os.Pipe is one guest-to-guest stream<u8>, and a read or write that must wait parks
// only its goroutine in the runtime's netpoller. It prints properties, and one order, never a time.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("pipe:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Phase 1: A parks reading; B sleeps, then writes "ping".
	aStarted := make(chan struct{})
	aGot := make(chan string)
	aDone := false
	go func() {
		close(aStarted)
		buf := make([]byte, 512)
		n, err := r.Read(buf)
		aDone = true
		aGot <- fmt.Sprint(string(buf[:n]), err)
	}()
	<-aStarted
	bSaw := make(chan bool)
	var slept time.Duration
	go func() {
		parked := !aDone
		t0 := time.Now()
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
		slept = time.Since(t0)
		parked = parked && !aDone
		if _, err := w.Write([]byte("ping")); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("write ping:", err)
		}
		bSaw <- parked
	}()
	got := <-aGot
	parked := <-bSaw
	fmt.Println("A got ping:", got == "ping<nil>")
	fmt.Println("B ran while A was parked:", parked)
	fmt.Println("slept >= 10ms:", slept >= 10*time.Millisecond)

	// Phase 2: B writes "pong" with no read pending, so its write parks; A sleeps, then reads it.
	aRead := false
	bWrote := make(chan bool)
	go func() {
		_, err := w.Write([]byte("pong"))
		bWrote <- err == nil && aRead
	}()
	time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	buf := make([]byte, 512)
	n, err := r.Read(buf)
	aRead = true
	fmt.Println("A read pong:", string(buf[:n]) == "pong" && err == nil)
	fmt.Println("B's write returned after A read:", <-bWrote)

	// Phase 3: B closes its end, and A reads the end of input.
	w.Close()
	n, err = r.Read(buf)
	fmt.Println("A read EOF after B closed:", n == 0 && err == io.EOF)
	r.Close()

	// Phase 4: two readers parked on two pipes; both writes complete at once, so two events are ready
	// together, and the order the readers run in is the netpoller's. Each pipe is used once first, so
	// that its buffers exist: a first read or write allocates, and an allocation can yield, which would
	// let a reader miss the write it was meant to be parked for.
	r1, w1, _ := os.Pipe()
	r2, w2, _ := os.Pipe()
	started := make(chan struct{})
	order := make(chan string, 2)
	for i, rr := range []*os.File{r1, r2} {
		go func() {
			b := make([]byte, 16)
			rr.Read(b) // the warm-up byte
			started <- struct{}{}
			n, _ := rr.Read(b)
			order <- fmt.Sprintf("%d:%s", i+1, b[:n])
		}()
	}
	w1.Write([]byte("a"))
	w2.Write([]byte("b"))
	<-started
	<-started
	w1.Write([]byte("one"))
	w2.Write([]byte("two"))
	fmt.Println("readers ran:", <-order, <-order)

	// Phase 5: a read abandoned at its deadline stays in flight, and the next read collects what it
	// read later, as net/http's abortPendingRead needs.
	r3, w3, _ := os.Pipe()
	r3.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Millisecond))
	n, err = r3.Read(buf)
	fmt.Println("read timed out:", n == 0 && os.IsTimeout(err))
	w3.Write([]byte("late"))
	r3.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
	n, err = r3.Read(buf)
	fmt.Println("next read got the late bytes:", string(buf[:n]) == "late" && err == nil)
	r3.Close()
	w3.Close()

	// Phase 6: closing a read end with its read still in flight cancels the read before dropping
	// the end, and the writer then sees a broken pipe.
	r4, w4, _ := os.Pipe()
	r4.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(time.Millisecond))
	r4.Read(buf)
	fmt.Println("closed a read end mid-read:", r4.Close() == nil)
	_, err = w4.Write([]byte("x"))
	fmt.Println("write after the reader closed fails:", err != nil)
	w4.Close()
}
